subject: BYO Key rotation: agent-side secret mirroring, telemetry, and VPC egress review

From: Rachel Chen <rachel.chen@fintech.io>

Subject: FinTechCo: BYO rotation approach + telemetry needs (staging mirroring question)

Hi Tessa / Monica / Kim,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — appreciate the clear breakdown of the private deployment options. As we start mapping our operational requirements for BYOK we hit a few areas where we need engineering guidance from Redwood before we finalize our network diagram. Two short asks:

1) We want to stage key rotations by mirroring a subset of secrets into a staging HSM (air-gapped) to validate live traffic behavior before cutover. Do you have an agent-side pattern (pull from customer KMS + push mirror) you recommend versus your control-plane-driven push?

2) We need telemetry hooks for rotation lifecycle events (rotate-start, rotate-complete, rollback) with per-tenant signing attestations. Minimal egress is a hard requirement — the audit team prefers signed rotation events uploaded to our S3 endpoint only.

I've attached a quick diagram and a spreadsheet with our proposed event fields. Could you confirm which of these are supported out-of-the-box and which need custom work? Also, any guidance on latency implications (token-lookup RTTs) when a staging mirror is live would be helpful.

Ideal timeline: decision this week so we can include it in our runbook and send to procurement.

Thanks,
Rachel Chen
Director, Security Engineering
FinTechCo

Attachments: ftco-byo-ops-diagram-v1.png (image), rotation-event-scheme.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinTechCo: BYO rotation approach + telemetry needs (staging mirroring question)

Rachel — thanks for the clear asks and the artifacts. Quick answers up front, then a short proposal for a low-risk pattern:

Short answers:
- Agent-side mirror (customer-controlled pull + local mirror) gives you the strongest network isolation and auditability. It also keeps final key custody under your operator controls.
- Control-plane push (Redwood-initiated) is easier to orchestrate for canary rollouts across hundreds of routes, but it requires an allowed egress path from the private deployment to our control endpoints and tighter SLA commitments.
- Telemetry: we can emit signed rotation events (JWT with attestation assertion) to a customer endpoint. We support webhooks and S3 push. Events include rotate-start, rotate-step(N), rotate-complete, rotate-rollback, operator-evict, and audit-checksum.

Proposal (recommended for FinTechCo staging):
1) Deploy a small rotation agent inside your VPC that pulls wrapped key material from your HSM (BYOK KMS) on a schedule. The agent mirrors keys into a staging HSM in the same VPC/subnet (no internet egress).
2) Redwood runtime routes a configurable percentage of production traffic to a staging pool (blue/green style) — we recommend starting at 1% for timing and cache-warm checks.
3) Rotation agent produces a signed rotation event bundle and writes to your S3 endpoint. Redwood polls the S3 location (or subscribes to a webhook you prefer) to learn rotation completion and then performs routing changes.

Notes on latency and caching:
- When staging mirror is active, expect an up to ~15–40ms p99 delta on first-token lookups for affected routes due to extra KV cache priming and attestation validation. Continuous traffic warms caches and this drops to single-digit ms.
- We suggest prefix-based cache invalidation to avoid full model KV flush during a rotate; we can provide a script for atomic prefix swap.

Action items for this week so we can lock the runbook:
- Monica: can you confirm operator IAM scope for the rotation agent (list minimal roles)?
- Kim: can your security team confirm the attestation JWT claim set in Rachel's spreadsheet? (we map to our runtime fields)
- Jonas: I'll need a short networking note on VPC egress rules and S3 presign policy.

I'll sketch a concise runbook and send it back as a single-page artifact for procurement. If you prefer, we can flip control-plane push for the production cutover and keep agent-mirror for staging only.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FinTechCo: BYO rotation approach + telemetry needs (staging mirroring question)

Rachel — quick IAM and operational notes below, flagged items where we need you to confirm your side:

IAM (rotation agent minimal scope):
- Read-only to KMS wrap/unwrap endpoints for the keys being mirrored (customer-side HSM).
- Write-only to staging HSM's key import endpoint (scoped to import token).
- PutObject to a dedicated S3 prefix for rotation events (we recommend path: s3://ftco-byo-rotate/events/<tenant_id>/).
- ListBuckets/HeadObject only if you plan to let Redwood poll (we can avoid listing via exact-key presigned uploads).

Operational safeguards we will implement on our side:
- Signed event verification: Redwood will verify the agent JWT signature and the attestation nonce before any routing change.
- Atomic routing swap: we will use a config flag that routes traffic to the whole staging pool only after successful event ingestion and health checks pass.
- Rollback window: route fallback can be automated for N minutes if p99 latency or error rate exceeds threshold.

Questions for FinTechCo (please confirm):
1) Will your staging HSM accept imported keys with the same key IDs as production, or do you want separate IDs and a mapping layer?
2) For attestation signing, do you control the private signing key inside your HSM, or will an HSM operator key be provisioned to the rotation agent?

I'll compile these into a one-page runbook and drop it into the Drive link.

—Monica
Monica Patel

All — thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed notes. Short answers to your clarifying questions below, then we can proceed: 

1) Staging HSM key IDs: we prefer separate IDs with a mapping layer. Ops wants to be explicit about what moved where.
2) Attestation signing key: will remain inside our HSM; the rotation agent will produce signed JWTs using an HSM-exposed signing operation (agent does not export private key material).

We confirm the S3 prefix and presigned-only uploads — we'll avoid list/head permissions. We'll also send a short network boundary diagram (VPC egress, NAT rules) for Jonas.

Next steps from FinTechCo:
- I'll share the final rotated-key ID mapping table in the Drive link by EOD tomorrow.
- We'll provision the agent IAM role with the minimal permissions Monica outlined.

Requested from Redwood for procurement runbook: the single-page runbook, an estimated latency delta table for first-traffic vs warmed cache (p50/p95/p99), and a short template for the attestation JWT claim set.

If you can drop those three artifacts into the Drive folder, procurement and security can sign off quickly.

Best,
Rachel
